# PLTR Technical Analysis (as of 2026-11-18)

## 1. Bottom line

PLTR is in a corrective downtrend inside a longer-term uptrend. The latest verified close is **156.67**, about 25% below the 2026-10-09 close of 209.05. It sits just above the 200-day SMA (153.83) and below every shorter-term trend gauge. Momentum is weak and deteriorating but not yet classically oversold. The key question is whether the 153–154 zone holds. That zone combines the 200 SMA with a cluster of recent intraday lows.

Verification note: the `get_indicators` outputs match the verified snapshot for every indicator the snapshot reports. MACD signal, MACD histogram and the Bollinger upper and lower bands come only from the snapshot. VWMA comes only from `get_indicators`, so the snapshot cannot confirm it. No discrepancies were found.

## 2. Indicators selected and why

I chose eight complementary indicators:
- **Trend structure:** close_10_ema, close_50_sma and close_200_sma cover short, medium and long horizons.
- **Momentum:** macd (with signal and histogram from the snapshot) and rsi.
- **Volatility:** boll (with upper and lower bands from the snapshot) and atr. PLTR has had large gaps and swings, so band width and risk sizing matter.
- **Volume confirmation:** vwma shows whether volume-weighted prices confirm the price trend.

## 3. Verified price action

Latest row (2026-11-18): open 158.25, high 158.44, low 153.50, close 156.67, volume 14,718,870.

- **Peak and decline.** Closes ran from 194.12 (10-07) to 209.05 (10-09), then 200.97 (10-14), 186.03 (10-16), and a lower-high rally to 201.72 (10-21). Closes were 196–199 through 10-29, then fell: 184.11 (10-30), 178.34 (11-02), 175.40 (11-03), 171.70 (11-04), and **154.99 on 11-05**, the lowest close in the window. The 11-05 intraday low was 152.60.
- **Gaps.** 11-03 opened at 168.18 against a prior close of 178.34. 11-05 opened at 166.71 against a prior close of 171.70. Both were gap-down opens.
- **Relief rally.** Price rose from 154.99 (11-05) to 172.40 (11-11), with a high of 175.41 that day. Volume faded, with 12.5M on 11-12 and 16.1M on 11-11.
- **Renewed weakness.** Closes were 167.99 (11-13), 160.39 (11-16), 156.56 (11-17) and 156.67 (11-18). The last three sessions retraced most of the bounce.
- **Retest.** The intraday lows of 153.91 (11-17) and 153.50 (11-18) sit just above the 11-05 low of 152.60. The 11-18 close of 156.67 is almost identical to the 11-17 close.
- **Volume.** Sell-off days in early November printed about 50M or more (53.1M on 11-03, 50.0M on 11-05). The recent decline from 11-16 to 11-18 came on only 14.7–17.8M shares. The latest bar's volume may not reflect a complete session, so treat it cautiously. The lighter volume is notable because the pullback is not showing the heavy-volume capitulation of 11-03 and 11-05.
- **Wider context.** The 08-04 surge (close 162.66 on 175M shares) started the advance toward the 200s. Price is now back below that session's close.

## 4. Trend: moving averages and VWMA

| Gauge | Value | Price vs. gauge |
|---|---:|---|
| 10 EMA | 165.71 | Price below, about 9.0 under |
| VWMA | 168.80 | Price below |
| Bollinger middle (20 SMA) | 176.61 | Price below |
| 50 SMA | 183.98 | Price below, about 27.3 under |
| 200 SMA | 153.83 | Price above, only about 2.8 over (1.8%) |

- **Short term is bearish.** The 10 EMA fell from 197.44 (10-27) to 165.71. Price is below it and the slope is still steeply negative, so rallies toward 165–169 face overhead supply from the 10 EMA and VWMA.
- **VWMA below the 10 EMA.** VWMA (168.80) has fallen from about 199 in late October, which is consistent with the downtrend carrying volume weight. It sits only slightly above the 10 EMA.
- **Medium term is rolling over.** The 50 SMA peaked at 186.90 on 10-30 and has drifted down to 183.98 in 13 sessions. It is not yet steeply falling.
- **Long term is intact but tested.** The 200 SMA is still rising slowly, from 152.11 on 10-05 to 153.83. The 50 SMA remains about 30 points above it, so there is no death-cross configuration. Price is hugging the long-term benchmark.
- **Structural read.** Price below the 10 EMA, 50 SMA and VWMA but above the 200 SMA is a pullback within a larger uptrend that is now at a decision point. A sustained close below the 200 SMA would damage that picture.

## 5. Momentum: MACD and RSI

- **MACD.** The MACD line is -8.03, the signal line is -6.03 and the histogram is -1.99. The MACD line crossed below zero between 11-02 (+0.55) and 11-03 (-0.85). It reached a local trough of -6.54 on 11-10, then fell to -8.03, the lowest value in the 45-day window. The histogram is negative and widening, so downside momentum is still expanding. There is no bullish crossover or momentum divergence yet. Price made a roughly equal low on 11-17/18 versus 11-05, but MACD is much lower, which is the opposite of a bullish divergence.
- **RSI.** RSI is 32.96, just above the conventional 30 threshold. It dropped to 25.42 on 11-05, bounced to 42.40 on 11-11, and has since fallen back to 32.83 (11-17) and 32.96 (11-18). That is a lower high on the bounce. In a downtrend RSI can stay in the 30s or go below 30, so the current reading is not a standalone buy signal. The earlier readings of 76.3 on 10-09 and 76.2 on 10-12 show how stretched the prior run was.

## 6. Volatility: Bollinger Bands and ATR

- **Bollinger Bands.** Lower band 145.21, middle 176.61, upper 208.02. Price is about 18% of the way up the band range, in the lower portion but not touching the lower band. The middle band has dropped from 197.48 (10-29) to 176.61 and is falling, which fits a downtrend where price is walking below the mean. The bands are wide at about 63 points, reflecting the large recent swings.
- **ATR.** ATR is 8.57, about 5.5% of the close. It peaked at 9.72 on 11-09 and has eased slightly. Daily ranges of 8–9 points are normal right now, so stops tighter than about 1 ATR are likely to be hit by noise.

## 7. Actionable observations for the decision-maker

These are scenarios, not a trade call.

**Key levels (from tool data):**
- Support: 153.83 (200 SMA) and the 152.60–153.91 intraday-low cluster (11-05, 11-17, 11-18). Below that, 145.21 (lower Bollinger band).
- Resistance: 165.71 (10 EMA), 168.80 (VWMA), about 172–175 (the 11-11 close of 172.40 and high of 175.41), 176.61 (Bollinger middle) and 183.98 (50 SMA).
- Caveat: the 11-05 low was followed by a rise to 172.40 by 11-11. That is one observation, not evidence of reliable support.

**Bearish scenario.**
- A close below about 152–153 would break both the 200 SMA and the retested lows.
- MACD and histogram are still weakening, and the 10 EMA and VWMA are still falling.
- The next reference is the lower band at 145.21, about 7% below the current close (arithmetic from the verified figures).

**Bullish or stabilization scenario.**
- Watch for a hold above 153.83, RSI turning up from the low 30s, and the MACD histogram shrinking toward zero.
- A reclaim of the 10 EMA (165.71) and then VWMA (168.80) would be the first sign that the short-term trend is repairing.
- The 11-06 to 11-11 bounce stalled below the Bollinger middle, which is now 176.61 and falling.

**Risk management.**
- At an ATR of 8.57, a 1.5 ATR buffer is about 12.9 points and a 2 ATR buffer is about 17.1 points.
- Any stop placed only just under the 200 SMA is within one day's typical range, so position sizing should reflect that.
- The tools show gaps of more than 10 points (11-03, 11-05, 08-04), so stops can be skipped on gap opens.

**What would raise confidence.** A close back above 165.71 and 168.80 on rising volume, a MACD histogram turning positive, or a volume-driven flush below 153 followed by a quick recovery.

- The price has dropped well below its 50-day average and now sits near the 200-day average. That is a short-term momentum break, and the 200-day (~$154) is the nearest technical support.

---

## 2. Income statement: growth is accelerating

- **Growth is speeding up.** YoY revenue growth went from 85% to 93% to 96% across the last three reported quarters. Sequential growth is about 19% per quarter (+18.5% in Q2, +19.5% in Q3).
- **Operating leverage is strong.** Operating margin rose from 33.3% to 46.9% YoY. Operating expenses fell from 40.6% of revenue (Q1) to 36.5% (Q3), derived as gross profit minus operating income.

It is still above the year-ago 82.5%, but the trend is worth watching. Operating margin has held flat at ~47% only because opex leverage offset it.
- **Net income exceeds operating income** in Q3 ($1,128M vs $1,085M), which points to interest income on the large cash and securities pile.

## 3. Cash flow: very high cash conversion

- **Operating cash flow is up about 145% YoY** over nine months.
- **FCF margin is ~52% in Q3** and ~56% over 9M 2026 (derived on $5.881B of nine-month revenue).
- **Capex is negligible**, at roughly 0.5% of revenue.
- **Financing cash flow is small** (+$20M over 9M 2026). There is no evidence of large buybacks, debt issuance or equity raises in this data. The tool provides no stock-based compensation or share count lines, so dilution can't be assessed here.
- **Cash movements:**
  - In Q2 the company put ~$1.48B into investments (investing cash flow was -$1,483M that quarter).
  - In Q3 investing was a net inflow of ~$371M.
  - Cash and equivalents rose from $2.03B to $3.62B.
- **Data discrepancy:** the vendor's TTM FCF is $2.65B. That is lower than the ~$3.29B nine-month FCF I derived from the filings, so the vendor figure looks stale or uses a different definition. I would trust the filing-based figure. On the vendor number, the FCF yield is ~0.7%. Annualizing 9M FCF gives ~1.2%.

Your best framing was "forward P/E 61.7x against ~79% EPS growth, so roughly 0.8x growth." Three problems with it:

If growth slows to 60% and the multiple falls to 25x, the result is also ~$370B. So you need 60%+ growth and a multiple that stays above 25x just to earn nothing over a year.

Even your preferred FCF figure gives a ~1.2% yield (~$4.4B annualized 9M FCF on $377.5B), and the vendor's number is lower. I don't have the 10-year yield, but with a hike priced at 92%, the risk-free rate isn't zero.

You note that a record quarter landed inside this drawdown. The data doesn't date the print precisely, but if it did, that cuts against you. When the best quarter in the data set can't hold the stock up, the good news was already in the price. And nobody here can say *why* the stock fell, because the news feed failed. You said equity grew 52% "funded by retained earnings rather than dilution." Check the bridge. Equity rose $3,841M from December to September, but 9M net income was only $3,061M. The FCF margin also flatters if SBC is added back. And ~$9.1B of current assets are neither cash nor labeled, so we don't know how much is receivables.

PLTR is a great business at a price that already assumes sustained acceleration, no margin slippage, benign rates, and no dilution drag. The data shows margin plateau, rising cost of revenue, a ~$780M equity gap we can't explain, a hawkish rate backdrop, and a chart where the bounce failed and momentum is still making new lows. Over to you, bull. Explain the $780M.
